what_its_for: Tetracycline is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as acne, chest infections, urinary tract infections, and certain sexually transmitted infections like chlamydia. It works by stopping bacteria from growing and multiplying in your body.
how_to_take: Take tetracycline by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Take it on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals for best results. Do not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking it to prevent throat irritation. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is completely cleared.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken 2 to 4 times a day, depending on the type and severity of your infection. Your doctor will tell you the exact dose and how long to take it. Never take more or less than prescribed. Doses are spaced evenly throughout the day — for example, every 6 hours if taking it 4 times a day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tetracycline at room temperature, away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use expired tetracycline — expired tetracycline can actually become harmful. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking tetracycline with dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt), antacids containing calcium, magnesium, or aluminum, iron supplements, or zinc supplements, as these can prevent the medication from being absorbed properly. Avoid prolonged sun exposure — tetracycline makes your skin more sensitive to sunlight and you can sunburn easily. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing outdoors. Do not take tetracycline if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid giving tetracycline to children under 8 years old, as it can permanently stain developing teeth yellow or gray.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe headache or blurred vision; painful or difficult swallowing; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of a new infection such as fever or worsening symptoms. Also call your doctor if your infection does not improve after a few days.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting tetracycline. However, it is very important to complete the full course of treatment as prescribed, even if you feel well. For acne, it may take several weeks to see noticeable improvement. Do not stop taking the medication early, as this can allow the infection to come back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Children under 8 years old: Tetracycline should NOT be used in children under 8 years old because it can permanently stain growing teeth and affect bone development. Pregnancy: Do not use tetracycline during pregnancy as it can harm the unborn baby, including causing permanent tooth discoloration and bone problems. Breastfeeding: Tetracycline passes into breast milk and should not be used while breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution and only under close medical supervision. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose. Older adults: May be more sensitive to side effects; follow your doctor's instructions carefully.
